page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is a compute-oriented virtual server featuring 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, driven by an Intel Xeon 8481C processor clocked at 2.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The platform allocates dedicated hardware threads with hyper-threading enabled. Memory capacity is provisioned at 8.0 GB, establishing a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware capabilities incorporate instruction set extensions including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance does not include integrated local storage or GPU accelerators, necessitating network-attached persistent disks for all non-volatile storage requirements.

Benchmark results demonstrate median single-thread performance alongside lower-tier multi-threaded aggregate throughput, reflecting the four-thread core boundary. Single-core evaluations record 1635.0 in Geekbench and 1620.59 in stress-ng, placing single-thread throughput in the middle performance bracket. In contrast, multi-core benchmarks reach 3703.0 in Geekbench and 3324.57 in stress-ng. Memory bandwidth delivers 27.54 GB/sec for uncached reads and 21.03 GB/sec for uncached writes, reflecting the constrained memory layout. Static web serving reaches 6.78 GB/sec, while in-memory operations achieve 4.43 million Redis SET operations per second.

In qualitative terms, the c3-highcpu-4 configuration provides access to modern Intel instruction sets without incurring the operational overhead of surplus memory. The principal design tradeoff is the low overall memory ceiling and core count, which restricts execution of large-scale in-memory datasets or heavily parallel compilation. The instance is suited for lightweight compute jobs, static web serving, continuous integration runners, and microservices requiring dedicated processor resources with advanced vector instruction capabilities.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-4 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 4 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, powered by a dedicated 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor with 2 physical cores and hyper-threading. The instance features a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, providing 2.0 GB of memory per vCPU, and integrates modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX. It includes no local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on attached storage volumes. Synthetic benchmarks place single-core execution within average tiers, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth fall into the lower quartile due to the compact core configuration. Network web serving achieves 6.78 GB/sec, and Redis operations reach 4.43 million operations per second. The server provides a balance for lightweight, compute-bound tasks that do not require extensive memory capacity, fitting workloads such as continuous integration workers, light API serving, and utility batch processing.
